# SSH Hardening: From Attack Chain to Six-Layer Defense in Depth

> A comprehensive open-source ebook on SSH brute-force defense, bastion host architecture, and Zero Trust remote access. By LeisureLinux. MIT License.

## What This Book Covers

This ebook provides a complete, production-ready SSH hardening methodology — from protocol-level cryptography to enterprise bastion architecture. It maps to CIS Benchmarks, NIST SP 800-53, and MITRE ATT&CK frameworks.

**Target audience**: Sysadmins, SecOps engineers, DevOps/SRE, security architects, and advanced Linux users.

## Core Framework: Six-Layer Defense in Depth

| Layer | Goal | Key Technologies |
|-------|------|-----------------|
| Layer 1: Reduce Exposure | Make the SSH service invisible to attackers | nftables, Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale SSH, VPN |
| Layer 2: Authentication Hardening | Prevent unauthorized access even if found | Ed25519 keys, FIDO2/YubiKey, TOTP 2FA, SSH CA |
| Layer 3: Access Control | Limit what authenticated users can do | AllowGroups, PAM, sudo, forced-command |
| Layer 4: Active Blocking | Penalize repeated attack attempts | fail2ban, CrowdSec, ipset, SSH blocklists |
| Layer 5: Intrusion Detection | Detect successful intrusions | auditd, Wazuh, osquery, AIDE, osquery |
| Layer 6: Audit & Response | Trace and contain damage | ELK/Loki, SIEM rules, incident response playbooks |

## Production sshd_config Hardening Snippet

```
# /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf
# Aligned with CIS Benchmark for OpenSSH

# Network
Port 22
AddressFamily inet
ListenAddress 0.0.0.0
Protocol 2

# Authentication
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
AuthenticationMethods publickey,keyboard-interactive
MaxAuthTries 3
LoginGraceTime 30
PermitEmptyPasswords no
ChallengeResponseAuthentication yes
KbdInteractiveAuthentication yes

# Access Control
AllowGroups ssh-users
DenyUsers root
MaxSessions 3

# Cryptography (OpenSSH 9.x recommended)
KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512
Ciphers chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr
MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com
HostKeyAlgorithms ssh-ed25519,ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com,rsa-sha2-512,rsa-sha2-256

# Session
ClientAliveInterval 300
ClientAliveCountMax 2
X11Forwarding no
AllowTcpForwarding no
AllowAgentForwarding no
PermitTunnel no
Banner /etc/ssh/banner

# Logging
LogLevel VERBOSE
```

## Key Recommendations

- **Disable password authentication entirely** — use Ed25519 keys minimum
- **Enable multi-factor authentication** — key + TOTP or FIDO2 hardware token
- **Deploy fail2ban or CrowdSec** — with aggressive bantime for repeat offenders
- **Use nftables to restrict SSH source IPs** — default-deny policy
- **Implement SSH CA** for organizations with >20 servers — eliminates authorized_keys sprawl
- **Consider Zero Trust** — Tailscale SSH or Cloudflare Access for cloud-native environments
- **Audit with auditd** — log all SSH session commands, not just login events
- **Rotate keys and certificates** — 90-day cycle for user certs, annual for host keys

## Attack Surface Analysis

- 20-30 million SSH services exposed on the public internet at any time (Censys 2023)
- Full IPv4 port-22 scan costs under $1 and takes minutes with Masscan/ZMap
- Credential abuse is the #1 initial access vector (Verizon DBIR 2024, ~24%)
- Slow-and-low attacks (1 attempt per 60-120s from distributed botnets) bypass basic fail2ban

## Compliance Framework Mapping

| Framework | Relevant Controls |
|-----------|------------------|
| CIS Benchmark for Linux | Section 5.2: SSH Server Configuration |
| NIST SP 800-53 | AC-2, AC-3, AC-7, AC-8, AC-17, AU-2, AU-3, IA-2, IA-5, SC-8 |
| NIST SP 800-123 | Guide to Securing Remote Access |
| DISA STIG | RHEL SSH STIG (V-207545 through V-207589) |
| MITRE ATT&CK | T1110 (Brute Force), T1021.004 (SSH), T1078 (Valid Accounts) |
| PCI DSS 4.0 | Requirement 8 (Authentication), Requirement 10 (Logging) |

## Book Chapters

1. **Why SSH Brute Force Is Still the #1 Threat** — exposure scale, attacker profiling, defense misconceptions
2. **Attack Side: Know Your Enemy** — ZMap/Masscan scanning, Shodan/Censys recon, dictionary attacks, Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK mapping
3. **Six-Layer Defense in Depth** (core chapter) — firewall, auth, access control, active blocking, IDS, audit & response
4. **Advanced Defense** — Port Knocking, SPA/fwknop, 2FA (TOTP/FIDO2), SSH CA, bastion hosts (Teleport/JumpServer), Zero Trust (Tailscale SSH/Cloudflare Access)
5. **Real-World Case Studies** — crypto-mining intrusion chain, APT slow brute-force, insider lateral movement
6. **Automated Defense** — hardening scripts, audit checklists, Cowrie honeypot deployment
7. **Mindset Evolution** — security trade-offs, post-quantum SSH, continuous learning
